檢校左僕射 is an acting Left Pushe of the Department of State Affairs (尚書省), not the Imperial Secretariat (中書省).

During the Qianning era he became commissioner of the Iron Forest Army; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Wang Xingyu, for merit he was given the additional title of acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and transferred to deputy commander of the inner guard.

During the Qianning era he became commissioner of the Iron Forest Army; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Wang Xingyu, for merit he was given the additional title of acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and transferred to deputy commander of the inner guard.
Same office mistranslation of 左僕射 as Imperial Secretariat rather than the Department of State Affairs.
In the fourth month he ordered Dewei to withdraw the army.
In the fourth month Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Dewei to withdraw the army.
The silent subject follows 武皇厭代 and 莊宗初立; rendering it as 'he' after Emperor Wu's death wrongly suggests Wu issued the recall.
In the fourth month he ordered Dewei to withdraw the army.
In the fourth month Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Dewei to withdraw the army.
Chinese 命德威班師 has a silent subject after Wu's death; the order belongs to the newly established Zhuangzong.

Liu Yan had meant to seize Linqing and cut the supply line from Zhen and Ding. When his army reached Chen Song Ford, Dewei's officers captured several dozen of his men, shaved the blades from their backs, bound them, and sent them back.

Liu Yan had meant to seize Linqing and cut the supply line from Zhen and Ding. When his army reached Chen Song Ford, Dewei's officers captured several dozen of his men, planted blades in their backs, bound them, and sent them back.
倳刃於背 means blades were stuck into the captives' backs to frighten Liu Yan, not that blades were shaved from their backs.

Earlier Liu Yan wished to hold Linqing to choke the Zhen and Ding supply route; marching to Chen Song Ford, Dewei sent officers who captured several dozen men, all with blades shaved on their backs, bound and sent back.

Earlier Liu Yan wished to hold Linqing to choke the Zhen and Ding supply route; marching to Chen Song Ford, Dewei sent officers who captured several dozen men, all with blades stuck in their backs, bound and sent back.
Literal English repeats the same mistranslation of 倳刃於背.

(From the Basic Annals of Taizu in the History of Liao: On the xinhai day of the third month of the second year of Shence the Khitan attacked Youzhou. Military Commissioner Zhou Dewei met them west of Juyong Pass with forces from You, Bing, Zhen, Ding, and Wei. They fought east of Xinzhou and routed the Jin army, taking thirty thousand heads.

(From the Basic Annals of Taizu in the History of Liao: On the xinhai day of the third month of the second year of Shence the Khitan attacked Youzhou. Military Commissioner Zhou Dewei met them west of Juyong Pass with forces from You, Bing, Zhen, Ding, and Wei. They fought east of Xinzhou and utterly defeated them, taking thirty thousand heads.
The Liao quotation's 大破之 does not name the Jin as the defeated party; the surrounding Jiu Wudai Shi and Tongjian reports have Dewei defeated, so inserting 'the Jin army' over-translates a pronoun.
At the opening of the Tongguang era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
At the opening of the Tongguang era he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
追贈太師 is a posthumous honorary appointment, not an enfeoffment (追封).
In the final years of Zhonghe, Hanzhi was driven out by Cai bandits, gave up his prefecture, and joined Ge Zhongshu.
In the final years of Zhonghe, Hanzhi was driven out by Cai bandits, gave up his prefecture, and joined Zhuge Shuang.
諸葛爽 is Zhuge Shuang; 'Ge Zhongshu' drops the surname 諸 and misreads 爽.
At the end of Zhonghe, Hanzhi was pressed by Cai bandits, abandoned the prefecture, and threw himself on Ge Zhongshu;
At the end of Zhonghe, Hanzhi was pressed by Cai bandits, abandoned the prefecture, and threw himself on Zhuge Shuang;
Same misrendering of 諸葛爽 as Ge Zhongshu.
After Ge Zhongshu died, Hanzhi was driven out by his own officers and fled to Huaizhou, his followers scattering. Cunshen then entered Emperor Wu's service.
After Zhuge Shuang died, Hanzhi was driven out by his own officers and fled to Huaizhou, his followers scattering. Cunshen then entered Emperor Wu's service.
諸葛爽 should be Zhuge Shuang, consistent with the Chinese.
When Ge Zhongshu died, Hanzhi was pressed by his own subordinate generals, went out to hold Huaizhou, and his followers scattered; Cunshen then returned to Emperor Wu.
When Zhuge Shuang died, Hanzhi was pressed by his own subordinate generals, went out to hold Huaizhou, and his followers scattered; Cunshen then returned to Emperor Wu.
Same personal-name error for 諸葛爽.

In the second month of the thirteenth year Liu Yan marched from Shen with his full strength to strike Weizhou. Cunshen pursued with the main army, routed the Bian forces at old Yuancheng, and helped recover Cao, Wei, Ci, Ming, and other prefectures.

In the second month of the thirteenth year Liu Yan marched from Shen with his full strength to strike Weizhou. Cunshen pursued with the main army, routed the Bian forces at old Yuancheng, and helped recover Chan, Wei, Ci, Ming, and other prefectures.
澶 is Chan (Chanzhou), not Cao 曹.

In the second month of the thirteenth year Liu Yan from Shen brought all his forces to surprise-attack our Weizhou; Cunshen with the main army followed on their heels, fought at the old Yuancheng, utterly defeated the Bian men, and followed in taking Cao, Wei, Ci, Ming, and other prefectures.

In the second month of the thirteenth year Liu Yan from Shen brought all his forces to surprise-attack our Weizhou; Cunshen with the main army followed on their heels, fought at the old Yuancheng, utterly defeated the Bian men, and followed in taking Chan, Wei, Ci, Ming, and other prefectures.

In the seventh month the Bian general Wang Zan crossed from Liyang to attack Cao Prefecture. Cunshen beat him back. Zan withdrew and encamped at Yangcun Ford, controlling the upstream crossing against us.

In the seventh month the Bian general Wang Zan crossed from Liyang to attack Chan Prefecture. Cunshen beat him back. Zan withdrew and encamped at Yangcun Ford, controlling the upstream crossing against us.
澶州 is Chan Prefecture, not Cao Prefecture.
In the seventh month Bian general Wang Zan crossed the river from Liyang to raid Caozhou; Cunshen resisted in battle, Zan withdrew, and encamped at Yangcun Ford, controlling our upstream.
In the seventh month Bian general Wang Zan crossed the river from Liyang to raid Chanzhou; Cunshen resisted in battle, Zan withdrew, and encamped at Yangcun Ford, controlling our upstream.
In the seventeenth year, when Liu Yan of Bian attacked Tong Prefecture, Zhu Youqian asked for our aid, and Cunshen and Li Sizhao were sent to the relief.
In the seventeenth year, when Liu Xun of Bian attacked Tong Prefecture, Zhu Youqian asked for our aid, and Cunshen and Li Sizhao were sent to the relief.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun (鄩 = Xún), not Liu Yan; the English personal name is a phonetic error.
He then had Wang Jian graze horses at Shayuan. When Liu Yan and Yin Hao learned of this, they withdrew with their troops and the siege of Tong was lifted.
He then had Wang Jianji graze horses at Shayuan. When Liu Xun and Yin Hao learned of this, they withdrew with their troops and the siege of Tong was lifted.
王建及 is the personal name Wang Jianji; 及 is not a conjunction. 劉鄩 is Liu Xun, not Liu Yan.

At the opening of Tongguang he was promoted Grand General of the Left with Three Excellencies ceremony, Acting Grand Preceptor, and Secretariat Director, with a fief of one thousand households and the title "Meritorious Subject, Fiercely Loyal, Upholding Heaven and Opening the Age."

At the opening of Tongguang he was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi (ceremonial equality with the Three Dignitaries), Acting Grand Preceptor, and Secretariat Director, with a fief of one thousand households and the title "Meritorious Subject, Fiercely Loyal, Upholding Heaven and Opening the Age."
開府儀同三司 is not 'Grand General of the Left'; it is the honorific office Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
Emperor Mingzong also sent his younger brother Yanqing, colonel of the Dragon Martial Guard, at speed to reassure the region.
Emperor Mingzong also sent Yanchao's younger brother Yanqing, colonel of the Dragon Martial Guard, at speed to reassure the region.
其弟 follows the Hedong narrative about Yanchao and matches Fu Yanqing, Cunshen's next son (s0227), not a brother of Mingzong.
Emperor Mingzong also sent his younger brother Yanqing, colonel of the Dragon Martial Guard, riding post to pacify them.
Emperor Mingzong also sent his (Yanchao's) younger brother Yanqing, colonel of the Dragon Martial Guard, riding post to pacify them.
Literal English makes Yanqing Mingzong's imperial brother; 彥卿 is Fu Yanchao's brother.

Before he could leave, his younger brother Yanrao, former prefect of Cao, pacified the mutinous Xuanyi army. The emperor was delighted and told Yanchao, "With your brothers' help I need fear nothing else. Go to Hedong for me and look after the old retainers there."

Before he could leave, his younger brother Yanrao, former prefect of Cao, pacified the mutinous Xuanwu army. The emperor was delighted and told Yanchao, "With your brothers' help I need fear nothing else. Go to Hedong for me and look after the old retainers there."
宣武 is the Xuanwu command, not Xuanyi.

Before he departed, it happened that his younger brother Yanrao, former prefect of Cao, pacified the mutinous troops of Xuanyi; Emperor Mingzong was pleased, summoned Yanchao and said to him, "With your brothers' strength I have nothing more to worry over—you go for me to Hedong and nurture the elders."

Before he departed, it happened that his younger brother Yanrao, former prefect of Cao, pacified the mutinous troops of Xuanwu; Emperor Mingzong was pleased, summoned Yanchao and said to him, "With your brothers' strength I have nothing more to worry over—you go for me to Hedong and nurture the elders."
宣武 should be Xuanwu, not Xuanyi.
In the first year of Changxing he was made military commissioner of Taiping, then soon transferred to garrison Anzhou.
In the first year of Changxing he was made military commissioner of Taining, then soon transferred to garrison Anzhou.
泰寧軍 is the Taining Army, not Taiping.
In the first year of Changxing he was appointed military commissioner of the Taiping Army, and soon transferred to garrison Anzhou.
In the first year of Changxing he was appointed military commissioner of the Taining Army, and soon transferred to garrison Anzhou.
泰寧 is Taining, not Taiping; 興元 is a false split of 長興元年.

At daybreak the deputy military commissioner of the prefecture Li Duan summoned prefectural troops to attack Foliu and the rest, killed them, the remainder fled to Huainan, and they captured Yanchao's subordinate generals Zhao Wen and twenty-six others and executed them.

At daybreak the deputy military commissioner of the prefecture Li Duan summoned prefectural troops to attack Foliu and the rest, killed them; the remainder fled to Huainan; they captured Yanchao's subordinate general Zhao Wen and twenty-five others, twenty-six in all, and executed them.
趙溫等二十六人 means twenty-six men including Zhao Wen, not Zhao Wen plus twenty-six.

Fragment of 開府儀同三司

ethnonym 蕃漢, not the Bian general Han

Author surname inside the book title only

unresolvedReferences.description: The second 十二月 after Dewei's Youzhou appointment is not restated with a year; the Liu Yan raid is attested in that month but the exact Western year is only sequential, not independently numbered.
Li Sizhao and Fu Cunshen appear only as Tiancheng temple companions; their own lifetimes are not dated in owned units.
